question: Can a sender's message let an independent receiver identify a private target among equally likely held-out semantic candidates?
scope: Deterministic task, role-view, and analytic no-message reference validation only. No language comparison or model inference is part of this revision.

task.meaning_space: 3 x 3 x 3 Cartesian product over shape, color, quantity
task.generalization_axis: all unary values and pairwise combinations are present in training; held-out triples are novel
task.candidate_support: all candidates are distinct held-out meanings
task.episode_sampling: For every candidate_count-sized subset of the held-out set, enumerate each member once as the private target.
task.candidate_order: A deterministic order is sampled from seed and candidate subset only; all target variants of a subset have identical order.
task.no_message_bayes_accuracy: 1 / candidate_count; exactly 0.2 for the default five-candidate task
task.sender_candidate_information: sender does not observe the receiver candidate set
task.ideal_zero_error_payload_floor: ceil(log2(9)) = 4 fixed-width bits for every candidate_count >= 2 because every target pair can co-occur in a receiver set
task.payload_floor_setup_assumption: shared target-index codebook is preinstalled; setup/distribution cost is excluded from the ideal payload floor and must be charged operationally

sender: protocol instructions added by a later frozen experiment
receiver: protocol instructions and shared training examples added by a later frozen experiment
role_boundary.gold_visibility: Never included in sender or receiver model input.

primary_endpoint_for_future_model_study: Exact receiver candidate_id selection, paired by episode_id.
validation_requirements: role ledgers have identical unique episode IDs
receiver rows contain no target label
target is exactly one candidate and is balanced within each candidate set
candidate order is recorded and gold target position agrees
the analytic no-message Bayes reference is recomputed from the declared sampling process
every candidate is a held-out meaning and all episodes share the frozen split hash
future_costs: complete sender and receiver input/output tokens
protocol training, prompt/codebook setup, negotiation, and reuse horizon
invalid output, semantic fidelity, and receiver task success separately
resource_policy: Local model inference remains subject to the frozen host-resource gate; this preregistration does not relax it.
novelty_boundary: This is a task/scorer fixture that operationalizes receiver-side utility for the project's experiments. Held-out composition and independent receiver evaluation are established prior methods; no novel benchmark or language claim is made.
